svg.title: W-01 Landing page wireframe
svg.text: Soundcheck learns how your subscribers and newcomers actually watch,
from your own videos, then predicts how a new cut will hold each of
them, with an honest margin of error, and which edits would help.
⛨ Read-only YouTube access 🗑 Delete everything in one step
HeroPreview: an example soundcheck, labelled as one
“Not a result yet” until it is
Open Channel and choose Disconnect and delete data.
How many videos do I need?
What happens to the cuts I upload?
Who can see my channel's data?
Footer: Soundcheck · How it works · What you get · Your data · Questions
Run a soundcheck before you publish
The page is rendered on the server from constants and two settings (MIN_TRAIN_VIDEOS,
MIN_VIEWS). It has no data to wait for, no empty state, and no error state of its own.
The views rule appears in the FAQ only when MIN_VIEWS > 0.
Soundcheck wants to: view your YouTube account · view YouTube Analytics reports
Hero. Signed out: Connect your YouTube channel starts Google sign-in (a server action, signIn("google") →
Three steps and four feature cards. Every claim on the page is true of the code (page.tsx comment).
The honesty section and the minimum video count are read from MIN_TRAIN_VIDEOS.
FAQ as native <details>; answers are built from NEWEST_VIDEOS, MIN_VIEWS and the evaluation split.
→ Connect your YouTube channel → Google consent → W-02 (an error page) or /app → W-03 / W-04
→ Open your channel → /app (routes by build state)
→ See how it works → #how on the same page
